items.title: Trump and Zelensky appear at loggerheads despite Oslo optimism
items.summary: The Ukrainian leader's hug with Steve Witkoff in the Norwegian capital is unlikely to dispel misgivings about US policy towards his country, writes Paul Adams.
items.content:
The hug that Trump envoy Steve Witkoff offered Volodymyr Zelensky ahead of talks in Oslo is unlikely to have dispelled the Ukrainian leader's misgivings about the current direction of US policy towards his war-ravaged country.

Zelensky posted a video of the moment on social media, with the message "Ukraine is working for peace. I thank our partners for their support!"

But given everything that's happened this month, does the Ukrainian leader still regard Donald Trump as a partner?

The two men have never been close – that much is obvious – but have they now fallen out once and for all?

Both in rhetoric and actions, the past ten days have seen evidence of a rupture as deep as any in their fractious relationship.

"Zelensky's not a good guy for us to deal with," Trump told Newsmax last week.

"Zelensky doesn't know what he's talking about," Trump told a reporter on Monday when asked what he thought of the Ukrainian leader's suggestion that striking a diesel deal with Russia put the US on the wrong side of history.

Such personal attacks are typical of Trump's sledgehammer approach to diplomacy. It's hard to know when to take them seriously.

In June, he lashed out at Israel's prime minister, saying Benjamin Netanyahu "has no f**king judgement". Four months later, he endorsed Netanyahu enthusiastically, calling him a "great warrior prime minister".

"Trump can always do another U-turn," says Ian Bond of the Centre for European Reform. "But this does look bad."

For his part Zelensky has generally been circumspect in how he describes his unreliable but vital American counterpart.

But this month his frustration has been clear. Addressing a US congressional delegation, he spoke of "decisions on the American side that are hard to explain between friends" and voiced the fear that "some political decision has been made to slow down support for us."

Answering Trump's charge that he represented the principal obstacle to a negotiated settlement, Zelensky sounded more exasperated than ever.

"We have welcomed literally EVERY attempt by our partners to end this war with dignity," he wrote on Telegram on Monday.

After their notorious televised bust up in the Oval Office in February 2025, at which Trump accused Zelensky of "gambling with World War III", the US suspended military assistance and restricted intelligence sharing.

The crisis only lasted a week. And when the Trump administration decided, later that year, that it no longer wanted to finance direct military assistance to Ukraine, a mechanism was put in place for European countries to pay for American equipment instead.

One exception, in the wake of this year's US war with Iran, has been badly needed US-made Patriot air defence missiles.

Amid a global shortage, the supply to Ukraine has slowed to a trickle, making it harder than ever for Kyiv to shoot down Russian ballistic missiles.

The Washington Post, quoting an unnamed Ukrainian official, said "only a couple" of Patriot interceptors remained in Ukraine's stockpile, and that the Trump administration had slowed down the process by which US allies seek approval to transfer their stocks.

Similar concerns have been voiced in the past, but the latest reports – not confirmed by US officials – come against an increasingly difficult backdrop for Kyiv.

Earlier this month, as Ukrainian negotiators arrived in Miami for talks with Trump's all-purpose envoys Witkoff and Jared Kushner, they were blindsided by the news that the president had just struck a deal with Vladimir Putin to open US markets to Russian diesel.

Experts questioned whether it would do much to drive down US petrol prices, ahead of congressional mid-term elections (the apparent motive), but as a signal of US displeasure over Ukraine's campaign of long-range strikes on Russian oil refineries and Washington's willingness to do deals with the Kremlin, it represented a stinging rebuke to Kyiv.

Last Friday, Trump went further, waiving wide-ranging sanctions on Russia just two days before they were due to take effect.

Trump said the sanctions contained in the Graham Act (named after the former South Carolina senator Lindsey Graham, a vocal supporter of Ukraine who died in July) would hinder his efforts to broker peace. But for Kyiv and its supporters this was another alarming sign that the White House was siding with the Kremlin.

"What the Trump administration is doing is providing carrots to the Russians and sticks to the Ukrainians," former US ambassador to Kyiv William Taylor told the BBC.

Kiriil Dmitriev, a senior Putin envoy, called it "an important and truly historic moment".

For Moscow, this felt like a welcome return to the "spirit of Alaska", a phrase much touted by Russian officials in the wake of the Trump-Putin summit in Anchorage in August 2025.

Adding to the impression that Trump is turning his back on Ukraine is the allegation – again not confirmed by Washington – that the US has restricted the flow of intelligence and interfered with Ukraine's access to Elon Musk's Starlink satellite internet service.

Amid an escalation in Russia's drone and missile war on Ukraine's cities, Kyiv says advance warning provided by US satellite intelligence has been lacking.

"We didn't receive it during ballistic attacks for three days," Zelensky told NBC News.

On 12 October five Russian S-400 missiles hit Kyiv, reportedly before air raid sirens or mobile alerts had sounded.

The US Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, denied there had been any pause in intelligence sharing, blaming a "software problem" for the temporary lack of early warnings.

Similar uncertainty surrounds Ukraine's access to Starlink .

A week ago, Ukrainian officials reported that the system was being throttled, with terminals unable to maintain connections at high speeds, making it harder for Ukraine's military to intercept fast moving Russian drones.

Since the summer, Ukraine has struggled to cope with a wave of attacks by advanced, jet-powered drones.

It's not clear where any order to limit Ukraine's use of Starlink – or its military grade equivalent Starshield – originated. Reuters reported that it came from the White House.

Rubio said "no-one at the White House ordered anyone to slow down internet."

But the fact that such suspicions surface so frequently points to the lack of trust that continues to infect US-Ukrainian relations.

Much of this has its roots in Donald Trump's seemingly long-standing mistrust of Ukraine as a whole - and Zelensky in particular.

A decade ago, Trump became convinced that Ukraine had tried to prevent him from becoming US president. Among a number of unfounded allegations was the suggestion that the US Democratic National Committee had a server hidden somewhere in Ukraine.

When Zelensky became president, three years later, he resisted Trump's demands that he investigate charges of election interference.

During a notorious July 2019 telephone conversation, Trump also asked Zelensky to investigate Joe Biden, the man who went on to defeat him in the 2020 presidential election. Again, Zelensky refused.

At the time, the White House was withholding $391m (£290m) in military assistance to Ukraine, a juxtaposition that ultimately led to Trump's first impeachment.

Whether Trump's resentment over these historic slights continues to inform his current policy towards Ukraine is an open question, but it's clear that the roller coaster of US-Ukraine relations has taken another stomach-churning dip.

Following the talks in Oslo, Witkoff is taking a set of updated proposals to St Petersburg. All eyes will now be on Putin.

Jonas Gahr Støre, the Norwegian leader, said the talks in Oslo had helped "to straighten out a few things."

"There's nothing to gain from… digging into what was said yesterday or a week ago," he said diplomatically.

Zelensky said the day had begun with a productive conversation with the US Secretary of State and indicated that the issue of early warning had already been fixed. He also sounded optimistic about Patriot missiles and Starlink.

Yet despite the optimistic tone, it's hard to get around the fact that Volodymyr Zelensky and Donald Trump appear, once again, to be at loggerheads.

items.title: La maledizione dei Kennedy: muore Kyle, la nipote di Bob ed Ethel
items.summary: Dedita all'istruzione, dal 2020 era paralizzata per una lesione alla spina dorsale
items.content:
Una nuova tragedia si è abbattuta sulla famiglia Kennedy, in quello che sembra l'ennesimo esempio della maledizione che da decenni infierisce sul clan. Kyle Kennedy, la figlia di Michael Kennedy e una dei 34 nipoti di Bob e Ethel Kennedy, è morta a 42 anni nella sua casa di Westwood, in Massachusetts.

I motivi del decesso non sono noti, ma Kyle era paralizzata nel 2020 per una grave lesione alla spina dorsale. "Sarà ricordata per la sua dedizione ai figli e per il suo sostegno a favore di una riforma dell'istruzione destinata ai bambini svantaggiati e alle persone con disabilità", si legge nel suo necrologio. Dopo aver conseguito una laurea in storia alla Georgetown University, Kyle Kennedy ha ottenuto due master sull'istruzione. Nel 2012 si è sposata con Liam Kerr, con il quale ha avuto tre figli. La coppia ha avuto due gemelli, Conor e Josie, ma la bambina è deceduta pochi giorni dopo la nascita. Due anni dopo Kyle e Kerr hanno avuto un secondo figlio maschio, Declan. Negli ultimi anni Kyle era costretta sulla sedia a rotelle in seguito a una lesione al midollo spinale. Da quel momento era diventata una sostenitrice dei diritti delle persone con disabilità. Il suo impegno l'ha vista anche testimoniare a un'audizione sulla discriminazione nell'assistenza sanitaria verso le persone con disabilità di fronte al governo del Massachussets. Già l'inizio della sua vita era però stato contrassegnato da una tragedia la morte del padre quando ancora era piccola per un incidente di sci. La tragedia di Kyle si aggiunge alle altre della storia della famiglia, con numerose morti premature: dall'assassinio di Jfk nel 1963 e del fratello Bob, nonno di Kyle, nel 1968; nel 1999 John Fitzgerald Kennedy Jr morì in un incidente aereo nei cieli di Martha's Vineyard. E solo pochi mesi fa, a dicembre scorso, Tatiana Schlossberg, figlia di Caroline Kennedy e nipote di Jfk, è morta all'età di 35 anni per una leucemia acuta.

items.title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge
items.summary: The lawsuit argues the White House exceeded its authority in imposing the latest tariffs on the country and caused "immediate harm to American businesses".
items.content:
US President Donald Trump is facing another legal challenge on tariffs after the group that successfully sued over his so-called "liberation day" import taxes filed a new lawsuit over the latest Canadian levies.

The White House imposed a 50% levy on some $20bn of Canadian goods after trade talks between the US and Canada broke down in August.

The Liberty Justice Center filed a suit on behalf of US food business Gellert Global Group, urging the US Court of International Trade to find the levies unlawful and to order refunds with interest for affected importers.

The lawsuit argues the White House exceeded its authority in imposing the tariffs and caused "immediate harm to American businesses".

Gellert Global Group is a third-generation family business that is paying 50% tariffs on cheese exported from Canada. The New Jersey-based firm is also facing retaliatory tariffs from Canada on American-made cheese it sells north of the border.

Co-chief executive Thomas Gellert said the firm had spent generations building relationships with suppliers and customers in the food industry.

"These tariffs disrupt those relationships overnight and create costs and uncertainty that ripple through the entire supply chain," he said on Tuesday.

The Liberty Justice Center is challenging the administration's use of Section 338 of the 1930 Tariff Act to hit Canadian goods from wine to dairy products and hockey sticks.

That section of the nearly 100-year-old Act is aimed at protecting US business against foreign discrimination, but the legal group is arguing that it does not allow the executive branch "to impose sweeping tariffs or import restrictions whenever a trade dispute arises".

The lawsuit seeks to challenge the White House's reliance on retaliatory tariffs imposed by Canada to justify its own duties under Section 338.

Canada has imposed a series of countermeasures against numerous US tariffs. Last month, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney matched the Section 338 US tariffs "dollar for dollar" after Trump imposed them for what he called "unequal treatment" of US cars, dairy and alcohol.

It also points out Section 338 requires a 30-day waiting period before levies can be imposed, but the tariff on products including cheese was added to the list just a week before tariff collection began.

Sara Albrecht, chief executive of the Liberty Justice Center, said the case was not about Trump himself but about the presidency.

"No president should have the power to pull a dormant statute off the shelf and use it to impose sweeping tariffs or import bans without the limits Congress required," she said.

The lawsuit argues that Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 has been superseded by Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

It also argues that if Section 338 still applies, the White House has not established the legal basis for the sweeping tariffs against Canada.

"The case is not an objection to tariffs as such. It asks who has the power to impose them and whether the executive branch followed the law Congress wrote," the Liberty Justice Center said.

The law group has also filed a motion for a preliminary injunction to block their collection.

It is the fourth case brought by the group against Trump's tariffs, including its successful case against the sweeping tariffs brought in under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) that were struck down in February this year.

Albrecht said the group had brought all the cases for the same reason: "the Constitution gives tariff power to Congress. The executive branch cannot keep moving the same policy from one statute to another and pretend the limits disappear".

'Half my business will be gone' - firms in Canada and US fear trade war

items.title: Da Ghali a Fedez, i rapper si schierano sugli scontri in piazza
items.summary: Marracash: "Mai inneggiato alla violenza. Avere i soldi non mi impedisce di lottare"
items.content:
La condanna della violenza, ma anche la voglia di dare voce al disagio sociale, al desiderio di riscatto di chi cresce tra insuccessi e sogno di ricchezza: il mondo del rap italiano, che ormai domina le classifiche e colleziona record di streaming (e di fatturato), si interroga sugli scontri che hanno scosso Milano e altre città d'Italia . E prende posizione con voci diverse, tra sostegno a una generazione a caccia di futuro, disapprovazione per il vandalismo gratuito e autocritica.

Ad aprire il dibattito è stato Marracash: "Con le buone non cambi le cose", ha scritto ieri sui social il rapper della Barona. Vicino alle sue posizioni è Sayf: "Ci dicono che il problema sono le manifestazioni violente, ma chi sta togliendo alle persone il diritto a un futuro dignitoso?", riflette l'artista, secondo a Sanremo 2026 con Tu mi piaci tanto. "Si dimentica la violenza di un sistema che mette il profitto sopra la vita e la dignità delle persone, perché il problema n on è la divisione tra destra e sinistra, ma quella tra chi sta sopra e chi sta sotto e noi siamo tutti dalla stessa parte: quella di chi sta sotto ". Quelle sulle diseguaglianze sociali "sono risposte che i giovani stanno cercando di ottenere ormai da un po'. Secondo me dobbiamo ascoltarli", sottolinea Ghali, che si dice "contento che le persone stiano scendendo in piazza a manifestare il proprio diritto e a cercare delle risposte" e invita a usare "questo tempo per parlare di chi sta manifestando pacificamente, perché è la vera cosa. Non distraiamoci". Per Nayt, "siccome in questo mondo viviamo insieme, a un certo punto, se non vedi l'altro, l'altro ti entrerà in casa per essere visto. Tutto questo finto benessere materiale ha reso borghesi anche i più poveri. Poverini e poveracci".

Opposta la valutazione di Fedez: "Conosco la frustrazione di una casa brutta in periferia, di un lavoro o di una scuola del ca**o, di non poterti comprare niente di bello. Conosco pure l'adrenalina di quando invece i soldi arrivano, la soddisfazione di poter far vedere agli altri dove sei arrivato. Per questo le vetrine del centro di Milano sono il bersaglio perfetto: rappresentano il simbolo tangibile di tutto ciò che a quei ragazzi è precluso. Vedo anche artisti e personaggi pubblici che celebrano la protesta , ci si uniscono come se ne facessero parte, senza rendersi conto che esposti in quelle vetrine ci sono anche loro. A promuovere quella idea di vita e di successo ci siamo noi. Siamo noi che andiamo alle sfilate, postiamo gli orologi di lusso, i viaggi e i vestiti". Un'allusione, probabilmente, a Ghali, tra i protagonisti delle ultime passerelle milanesi. Luchè sceglie il suo brano Se non ci fosse la rabbia e scrive "Non voglio unione / Voglio divisione / Combatto con chi ha / La mia stessa missione", mentre Nerone invita a distinguere tra "milioni di persone" che "stanno protestando pacificamente per cercare di farsi sentire da sti merda mangiasoldi" e "400 clown minorenni con le squalo e i buchi nel cervello" che "hanno sfondato negozi e auto come le peggiori delle bestie".

Se Guè e Artie 5ive siglano con il loro like il post di Marracash, quest'ultimo risponde alle critiche di chi ha letto nelle sue parole un incitamento alla violenza : "Ok, mi sono preso una vagonata di merda, ci sta, me lo aspettavo", scrive oggi in un lungo post. Ma "un paio di cose non mi stanno bene" , spiega. "La prima è che non ho mai inneggiato alla violenza", "ma quando questa violenza succede, bisogna farsi delle domande", perché pur nella follia del gesto è sintomo "di un fallimento della società di cui tutti siamo responsabili" . "Un risentimento crescente sta maturando in tutti", "per ora riguarda le classi più deboli e ai margini, le periferie e le seconde generazioni, ma sta crescendo anche nel ceto medio che manifesta pacificamente". Marracash respinge anche "la retorica del 'tu hai i soldi, non puoi parlare'". "Aver fatto i soldi non cancella più di metà della mia vita e soprattutto non mi impedisce di lottare per un mondo più equo e più giusto per tutti, né di lottare per questo".

items.title: Cornell Jane Doe says embattled university head doubted her gang-rape allegation
items.summary: As a no-confidence vote looms, Cornell says the characterisation of the head's reaction is "incorrect".
items.content:
A former Cornell student who alleges she was gang-raped at a fraternity house has said she felt "unsupported and disbelieved" by the university president.

Known anonymously as Jane Doe, she has written a letter accusing President Michael Kotlikoff of asking why she waited several weeks to report the incident.

The Ivy League institution in upstate New York says her account of the Cornell head's reaction is "incorrect".

She addressed her letter to campus faculty who will hold a rare vote this month on Kotlikoff's leadership. Doe filed her lawsuit last month alleging she was raped by several men in October 2024 at a Chi Phi fraternity party.

All seven former fraternity members accused by Doe have denied wrongdoing when contacted by the BBC's US partner CBS. None has been charged with a crime.

Doe reported the alleged assault to campus police, and the local prosecutor declined to bring charges at the time, but the case has since reopened .

Responding to Doe's initial allegation, Cornell said it had opened an internal investigation, as well as a civil rights inquiry.

What we know about Cornell University frat house rape investigation

In a two-page letter dated 14 October and obtained by the BBC, Doe told the faculty senate that after she reported the alleged rape, she received "a second-hand account" of Kotlikoff's reaction and that his "initial response" was "along the lines of, 'Why did she wait so long to report it?'"

Doe reported the alleged assault to campus police on 8 November, about three weeks after the fraternity party.

She noted that Kotlikoff had a conversation with the then-president of her sorority and that other staff members were present, at least one of whom "appeared distressed" by the college president's question.

Doe said in her letter: "It diminished my confidence in the administration's ability to approach my experience with the understanding, sensitivity, and fairness I had hoped for and expected from what had been my dream school."

She said she wrote the letter so that faculty "can make an informed choice" ahead of their 28 October vote on whether to express no confidence in Kotlikoff's leadership.

The university confirmed receipt of the letter from Doe's lawyer.

But in a statement to the BBC, a Cornell spokesperson said: "The second-hand account of the question asked by President Kotlikoff in a January 2025 meeting in the letter is incorrect, based on a documented first-hand account."

The spokesperson said Kotlikoff's question about the delay in reporting the alleged rape "was directed at bystanders who did not use Cornell's anonymous tip line, despite ongoing social media activity about the incident in October 2024".

"He was not questioning Jane Doe's reporting," the spokesperson said.

Kotlikoff, who has led the Ithaca-based institution for 26 years, was grilled by the faculty senate last Wednesday.

Staff said they were "deeply disturbed" by his handling of the case and accused him of lacking an "emotional response", according to recordings obtained by the BBC.

Kotlikoff highlighted changes the university had introduced as a result of Doe's allegations, including banning fraternity parties.

"We are all extraordinarily upset by the events at Cornell in October of 2024," he said.

The faculty senate, a governing body composed of professors and other academic staff at Cornell, scheduled their no-confidence vote for 28 October.

In recordings of the meeting, faculty said sexual misconduct on campus was a systemic problem that demanded "systemic attention".

Paul Ortiz, a labour history professor who sponsored the no-confidence resolution, said students had told faculty they "feel unsafe walking to the library after dark".

He accused Cornell of treating rape "as more of a 'PR problem' than a heinous crime".

Cornell case highlights 'draining' maze for victims to report campus sex assaults

Si vede, non si vede: la piega che hanno preso le discussioni sull'iPhone Duo a partire dalla sua presentazione di settembre, e in attesa dell'inizio delle spedizioni fissato per il 23 ottobre, ha avuto a che fare proprio con la piega, quella del display interno. Apple ha cercato di minimizzarla, e dagli hands-on sembra che abbia fatto un buon lavoro, sfruttando la pellicola nano-texture opaca per ridurne la visibilità (sacrificando però la vivacità dei colori a schermo).

SOTTO PRESSIONE

Ma c'è un video, condiviso dal noto leaker Ice Universe, che evidenzia un aspetto che nessuna anteprima del dispositivo aveva ancora sottolineato. Ovvero il comportamento della zona del display interno corrispondente alla piega quando viene sollecitata.

BREAKING！A shocking new discovery about the iPhone Duo's foldable display! According to Weibo user Kang, the screen around the iPhone Duo's crease is surprisingly SOFT to the touch. When pressed with a finger, the surface can even develop visible WRINKLES! This is something we've never seen mentioned in previous reviews of foldable phones. Even more interesting, Kang claims this behavior is common across multiple units. Could this be related to Apple's rumored variable-thickness ultra-thin glass (UTG), with a thinner central folding region and thicker surrounding areas? If so, Apple may have adopted a radically different approach to managing stress around the fold. The engineering behind this display could be far more interesting than we initially thought. items.title: Show HN: SimCity, but with Permits
items.summary: Article URL: https://permit.petercai.com/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50170593 Points: 733 # Comments: 357
items.content:
You are the mayor. You know exactly what this city needs. Now get it past the zoning board, the neighbors, the appeals court and the next election.

Permit Pending is a city simulation in the spirit of the classics, with one difference: you are not a god. You are an elected mayor. Every apartment block, bus lane and factory goes through hearings, reviews, objections, lawsuits and appeals. The economy underneath is real. The neighbors are not always rational. Win the argument, or win the election. Ideally both.

A typical case from your inbox. The economic answer was obvious. The political path was not.

New housing lowers rents and angers homeowners. New industry brings jobs and smog. Better transit attracts development, and development attracts opponents. Fix one problem and you create a new group of voters who are angry about it.

Your inbox fills with applications, controversies and recurring characters. Negotiate concessions at public hearings, win votes on a seven-seat council, and spend your political clout wisely. Some cases last longer than your term.

Residents have ages, incomes and homes. Businesses hire, grow and leave. Land values, rents, jobs, taxes and services all connect. The city keeps changing while you are stuck in committee.

High-turnout groups have more power than their numbers suggest. Know who votes.

Heatmaps, graphs and plain explanations show why voters are angry and which decision did it.

The Gazette reports your successes, your scandals and your parking minimums.

No campaign and no win screen. The city goes on as long as the voters let you.

Start with a hamlet at a crossroads, or inherit somebody else's problems.

A hamlet at a crossroads and empty streets waiting for zoning.

Housing demand and homeowners who are getting very organized.

A mature economy, severe land-use conflict and very entrenched interests.

"We have filed an appeal on procedural grounds. The procedure is the point."

No. The game runs in your browser. Saves stay on your computer, and after the first visit the game also works offline.

A desktop or laptop with a current browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari). A mouse helps.

Not exactly. It's a sandbox. Your goal is the city you want, and your challenge is to stay in office long enough to build it.

items.title: Gwyneth Paltrow al suo primo ruolo da protagonista assoluta in una serie tv
items.summary: Nel dramma thriller The Apology prodotto da A24 e ordinato per due stagioni da Netflix
items.content: Per la prima volta nella sua carriera, Gwyneth Paltrow reciterà da protagonista assoluta in una serie tv. L'attrice premio Oscar sarà Evelyn Amspoker, una madre distrutta dal dolore per il figlio, ucciso 18 anni prima in un caso irrisolto, nel dramma thriller 'The Apology', prodotto da A24 e ordinato per due stagioni da Netflix. La serie è diretta dal premio Oscar Thomas Vinterberg (Un altro giro), mentre la sceneggiatura è dello showrunner Joe Murtagh. Quando uno sconosciuto si fa avanti e confessa l'omicidio, la giustizia sembra possibile, tuttavia Evelyn e suo marito Caleb scoprono che l'assassino potrebbe ottenere una pena ridotta e decidono di farsi giustizia da soli, anticipa la sinossi riportata da Variety. Mentre la filmografia dell'attrice vanta ruoli iconici come in 'Emma', 'Sliding Doors', 'Shakespeare in Love' e 'Il talento di Mr. Ripley', la sua carriera televisiva è stata meno gloriosa. Paltrow ha partecipato, nell'arco di cinque episodi, a 'Glee' nel ruolo di Holly Holiday e ha avuto un ruolo secondario nella serie Netflix di Ryan Murphy 'The Politician', ma non ha mai recitato come protagonista in una serie televisiva.

items.title: Occhi chiusi? Ora su Adobe Lightroom mobile ci pensa l'AI ad aprirli
items.summary: Bastano pochi tocchi.
items.content:
Occhi aperti, c'è una novità su Lightroom mobile, la versione dell'app per iOS, Android e iPadOS disponibile ormai da anni (presto arriverà anche Adobe Premiere). E ha a che fare proprio con gli occhi, quelli chiusi, uno degli elementi che più comunemente può rovinare una bella foto. Adobe ha infatti introdotto uno strumento, disponibile su tutte le piattaforme mobile, che consente proprio di correggere questo difetto.

OPEN EYES

Il funzionamento è semplice e immediato: quando Lightroom riconosce una persona o un gruppo di persone con gli occhi chiusi, ecco che mostra direttamente sull'immagine una inedita azione rapida denominata "Open Eyes". A questo punto è sufficiente un tocco per avviare la correzione: nessun intervento manuale, ovviamente, pensa a tutto l'AI generativa.

La feature non è del tutto inedita nel mondo Adobe. Photoshop Elements permette da anni di intervenire sugli occhi chiusi, recuperando però il risultato da un'altra fotografia della stessa persona. Ma se cambiano l'illuminazione, l'espressione o l'angolazione del viso, il risultato può apparire poco naturale.

Il miglior top gamma Android? Oppo Find X9 Pro, compralo al miglior prezzo da Amazon Marketplace a 1,079 euro.

items.title: Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 300 people, sources say
items.summary: A truck carrying people to a funeral and a market alleged to be supplying fuel to the RSF were targeted.
items.content:
Sudan's army has been accused of launching several drone strikes that have reportedly killed more than 300 people, including dozens travelling to a funeral.

The death toll from strikes in two areas of West Kordofan state on Sunday evening was 150, sources told the Sudan War Observatory, which tracks the conflict that erupted in 2023 between the army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).

In Abyei, a disputed border area between Sudan and South Sudan, 153 people were killed when drones hit a market on Monday, the region's information minister said.

A military source told the BBC the army had carried out the Abyei attack, saying the market was a fuel supply site for the RSF.

The attack has raised tensions between South Sudan and Sudan, which jointly administer Abyei, as they both claim ownership to the oil-rich region in a dispute that has remained unresolved since South Sudan ceded in 2011.

South Sudan has summoned Sudan's ambassador to lodge a formal protest. There are fears the conflict could spill across the border.

Drones hammer Sudan's gold and oil zone - the pivotal new front line

Despite a partial arms embargo on Sudan, foreign countries have been supplying both the army and the RSF with drones and they are increasingly becoming the weapon of choice in the conflict.

The war has created one of the worst humanitarian crises in the world, killed hundreds of thousands of people and forced more than 14 million from their homes.

"We are alarmed by the continued deadly drone strikes across the country that are killing civilians, including children, and that are disrupting essential services," UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said on Monday , external .

The rising use of armed drones came as 20 million people faced acute hunger, with a rising risk of famine in parts of the western region of Darfur and Greater Kordofan, he said.

Greater Kordofan comprises three states and is a vital axis linking Darfur, controlled by the RSF, to the capital, Khartoum, now in army hands.

The wave of drone attacks started on Sunday evening and, according to the Sudan War Observatory, it is likely they were launched from the army-held city of Kadugli in South Kordofan state.

A truck carrying around 200 mourners which had travelled from an area north of Abyei was hit as it arrived in the town of Al-Dabab in West Kordofan, the monitoring group said.

Sources told the group that 145 people were killed and a tent where mourners at the funeral had gathered was also hit, killing five others. A further 150 people were injured in the attacks, it said.

Army drones also bombed a market in the town of Al-Mujlad in West Kordofan on the same evening, according to the Sudan War Observatory, which said the exact number of deaths and injuries were not yet known.

Sudan's army has not responded to the allegation it carried out these strikes, but said it did not attack civilians even if they believed there were RSF fighters amongst them.

The attack in Abyei, which borders West Kordofan, took place on Monday around 11:30 local time (09:30 GMT) targeting Amiet Market around 10km (six miles) from Abyei town, the region's Information Minister Yohana Akol Ngor told Radio Tamazuj, which broadcasts from the Netherlands to audiences on the Sudan-South Sudan border.

On Tuesday, the minister confirmed to the Associated Press and Reuters that the death toll had risen from 73 to 153 people.

"It is a horrible and shocking situation," AP quotes him as saying.

BBC Verify has studied satellite images that show extensive burnt buildings in the north-east corner of Amiet Market, which is also known in Arabic as Al-Na'am Market. Older images from the area show it is usually full of trucks.

It has also verified footage filmed near the market that shows a large plume of smoke, at least one petrol tanker and someone talking about five missiles being fired. Another verified video shows two massive, separate fires coming from buildings near that section of the market.

"The market was completely destroyed. The bombing spread terror and fear among the local population," market trader Fadlallah Adam Hamouda told BBC Arabic's Middle East Daily.

Another trader told the BBC the attack had come as shock as UN peacekeepers have been in Abyei since 2011 - with more than 2,800 uniformed personnel currently deployed.

"Our area is a weapons-free zone under United Nations protection, yet it was targeted by drones," he said.

"The attack caused extensive material damage after the fuel market was struck, sparking a massive fire that spread to nearby homes."

Earlier, Ngor told Reuters that emergency workers had struggled to retrieve the bodies because of fires caused by the strikes.

On Monday, medical charity Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) said it had also received people wounded in the attack at Ameth Bek Hospital in Abyei town.

"So far we received over 20 patients, including several critical cases. Patients with burns were also admitted. We are providing surgical services and wound dressing, along with other emergency care," MSF's Christian Lindauer, the charity's manager at the hospital, said in a statement.

Meanwhile, a drone strike near the airport in Khartoum on Monday has killed four people, including three children, the AFP news agency reports, quoting a medical source.

It also cited a military source as saying air defences in the Sudanese capital had downed several other drones launched by the RSF towards the airport.

Fighting in Kordofan, a strategic area rich in gold and oil, has intensified over the last year after the army regained control of Khartoum from the RSF.

items.title: What shall I teach my son?
items.summary: Article URL: https://stevekrouse.com/ends Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50169707 Points: 363 # Comments: 431
items.content:
Yesterday, the title The End of Education by Neil Postman called to me from my bookshelf, whispering that it might be the right book at the right time. It was. Published in 1995, it was surprisingly appropriate balm for the soul of a confused programmer and soon-to-be father.

My wife and I are expecting our first child. My economically valuable skillset – programming – suddenly feels less valuable. What shall I teach my son? And to what end?

Mr. Edison says That the radio will supplant the teacher. Already one may learn languages by means Of Victrola records. The moving picture will visualize What the radio fails to get across. Teachers will be relegated to the backwoods. With fire-horses, And long-haired women; Or, perhaps shown in museums. Education will become a matter Of pressing the button. Perhaps I can get a position at the switchboard.

– Quoted in The End of Education by Neil Postman, quoting Teachers and Machines: The Use of Technology Since 1920 by Larry Cuban

Books will soon be obsolete in the public schools… Our school system will be completely changed inside of ten years.

Back in 2013 , I boldly predicted that MOOCs would upend education. Ah, my past self, you sweet summer child.

Nassim Nicholas Taleb has helped me appreciate the staying power of staying power, sometimes called The Lindy Effect . Merely staying alive implies some anti-fragility to adapt and survive. Consider that Harvard, Yale, and Princeton were founded to educate the clergy. From The End of Education:

In the Western world, beginning in the thirteenth century and for five hundred years afterward, that God was sufficient justification for the founding of institutions of learning, from grammar schools, where children were taught to read the Bible, to great universities, where men were trained to be ministers of God.

Schools survived what happened to religion. It should be no surprise that they’ve survived the radio, motion pictures, and the internet.

We typically confuse why something claims it exists, ie to glorify God, vs the forces that actually perpetuate it, which are subtler, we’d prefer not spoken aloud, and more prosaic, ie endowments, prestige, and needing someone to watch one’s kids.

It has been a surprisingly good bet that schools will continue to exist in roughly their current form for many years to come. Ironically, there also seems to be some staying power to technologists boldly (and so far incorrectly) doubting the staying power of schools! I myself have contributed to this grand tradition multiple times, and find myself at risk of doing it yet again.

Surely this time must finally be different, right? We have captured intelligence in a bottle, and you’re telling me that “Ok class, turn to page 17” and “Does anyone know how to solve for x” are still going to be around in the 2030s?

There are many shifting purposes to education, which underpin how it has survived this long. As the times change, so do its purposes shift and adapt, such as:

I once tried to come up with a single-word purpose for education, and I landed upon the word “resourceful”, because I reasoned that if you “were able to use arbitrary resources to uncover and solve problems”, you had no more need for schooling. In the age of Google, email, and the internet, a person was educated when they could wield them. But now I see my vision of resourcefulness perfected in the AI agent and its tool loop. Maybe resourcefulness will go the way of the Dewey Decimal System which in turn supplanted memorization and an oral tradition.

Imagine education as a table held up by its many purposes. I didn’t realize how centrally important “the ability to earn a living” was for me until it started to wobble. A big reason is because I’m looking for a more objective arbiter of “good” in education. Education’s own tests and measures can feel stifling. The market offered a counterpoint. Steve Jobs and Bill Gates were college dropouts, but the market deemed them good. Now that I think of it, apparently Einstein was a mediocre student, but his contributions to science were his way out. With recent advances in AI mathematics, both of these paths to glory are under fire. Clara Collier makes similar points in her exceptional essay “ After Work, We’ll Have Each Other .”

If AI takes our ability to contribute, what’s left for our children?

Neil Postman offers a few suggestions for positive purposes for education that I found heartening, not mainly for their content, but for the fact that it’s possible to make up new purposes for education and advocate for them. My favorite suggestions of Postman’s are:

Spaceship Earth – we’re all in this together; let’s take care of each other and our planet

The American Experiment – let’s revive our sense of wonder, curiosity, and responsibility about what America is and can be

The World Makers – as a student of McLuhan, Postman would be remiss if he didn’t invite students to make the tools and narratives that thereafter make us

At the risk of going too meta, I do strongly believe in Postman’s point (in his other education book, Teaching as a Subversive Activity ) that “the medium is the message.” That the way we teach what we teach is often more important than the what . And likewise, I believe in Dr. Alfie Kohn’s notion that we should relate to our educational charges as humans, not objects – “doing with” vs “doing to”. Thus, I believe it may be most honest and effective to invite our children to help us craft the purpose for their education as we figure it out together.

items.title: Il pg di Cassazione: 'No allo stop dell'ex Ilva, bilanciare salute e produzione'
items.summary: Birritteri: 'La pericolosità dell'amianto è indiscussa ma la Corte di Appello di Milano desume il pericolo ma non lo accerta'
items.content:
"Quello che manca nel decreto della Corte di Appello di Milano che ha stabilito" lo stop dell'area a caldo dell'ex Ilva di Taranto "è il bilanciamento fra tutela della salute e produzione industriale". E' quanto ha ribadito oggi in aula, davanti alle sezioni Unite Civili della Cassazione, il sostituto procuratore generale, Luigi Birritteri, nel corso dell'udienza in cui si sono discussi i ricorsi presentati dalle aziende Ilva Spa, Acciaierie d'Italia e Acciaierie d'Italia Holding contro lo stop dell'attività produttiva dell'area a caldo.

Tema centrale, ancora una volta, il delicato equilibrio tra tutela della salute pubblica e prosecuzione dell'attività industriale. Per Birritteri "la pericolosità dell'amianto è indiscussa ma la Corte di Appello di Milano desume il pericolo ma non lo accerta". Ma dopo la requisitoria del pg interviene il senatore Mario Turco, vicepresidente del Movimento 5 Stelle, annunciando di aver depositato un'interrogazione al ministro della Giustizia Carlo Nordio sulla posizione di Birritteri.

"Non intendiamo mettere in discussione l'autonomia della magistratura né formulare accuse preventive. Ma proprio a tutela della sua indipendenza riteniamo indispensabile chiarire se siano state adeguatamente valutate eventuali ragioni di astensione", sostiene Turco che richiama circostanze riportate dalla stampa, secondo cui Birritteri avrebbe ricoperto incarichi al Ministero della Giustizia durante il mandato di Angelino Alfano.

Nelle scorse settimane la Procura generale aveva depositato una memoria con cui chiede un accoglimento parziale delle impugnazioni avanzate dalle società, soffermandosi soprattutto sulla vicenda relativa alla presenza di amianto nei cowpers degli altiforni. Secondo il Pg, la normativa vigente non prevederebbe un obbligo generalizzato di rimozione integrale di tutti i materiali contenenti amianto entro agosto 2023, indipendentemente dal loro stato di conservazione e dalla tipologia degli interventi richiesti.

Un altro capitolo riguarda le emissioni e il presunto pericolo collegato alle polveri sottili. Sul punto, la Procura generale ritiene che il provvedimento impugnato abbia ricavato l'esistenza di rischi gravi per ambiente e salute da dati epidemiologici riferiti a periodi ormai risalenti e da scenari produttivi non più attuali. Nelle conclusioni, la Procura generale sostiene anche che il richiamo al principio di precauzione non possa tradursi nell'applicazione di parametri diversi da quelli fissati dalla legge e chiede pertanto che vengano accolte le ulteriori censure mosse dalle società rispetto alle motivazioni che hanno portato al fermo degli impianti.

Di segno opposto la posizione degli undici cittadini assistiti dall'associazione Genitori Tarantini, intervenuti nel procedimento. In una memoria i loro difensori Maurizio Rizzo Striano e Ascanio Amenduni contestano le conclusioni del Pg e difendono la legittimità della decisione assunta dalla Corte d'Appello di Milano. Per i legali, infatti, "la continuità produttiva non può prevalere incondizionatamente sui beni costituzionali protetti".

La memoria delle parti civili punta a dimostrare come il rischio sanitario sia stato adeguatamente documentato e come il provvedimento impugnato individui due distinti profili di pericolo, rappresentati dalla presenza di amianto e dalle emissioni di polveri sottili. Secondo questa impostazione, ciascuno dei due elementi sarebbe autonomamente sufficiente a giustificare l'intervento disposto dai giudici milanesi. Al termine dell'udienza, i giudici si sono riservati la decisione che verrà quindi notificato alle parti.

items.title: Google open-sources TorchTPU, a native PyTorch back end for TPUs
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/google-pytorch/torch_tpu Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50169053 Points: 323 # Comments: 74
items.content:
This project provides a PyTorch backend for Google's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), enabling users to run PyTorch models and operations on TPU devices. It includes custom ATen kernels for various PyTorch operations, a compilation cache for optimizing execution, and examples for distributed training and model inference.

A user guide is available at https://torchtpu.readthedocs.io/ . This is a static version of the interactive notebooks. They are available in the docs folder.

The notebooks are Marimo (similar to Jupyter). They can be run with marimo edit file.py and then you can access them in your browser. You will need to be running this from a TPU VM, a v6e GCE instance is easiest.

The same instructions are available in the user guide linked above.

TorchTPU's Python version support policy matches PyTorch's Release Compatibility Matrix . Currently, Python 3.11+ is supported. See the Python Version Support Policy for more details.

Install the latest public release ( 0.2.0 on PyPI ) (for uv prepend uv to all pip commands):

All OSS Bazel builds default to optimized mode ( -c opt ) automatically via .bazelrc . Unoptimized builds ( -c fastbuild , -c dbg ) can degrade performance and are not used for wheel builds. If you are developing or debugging C++ code and explicitly want an unoptimized wheel, pass --//:allow_unoptimized_wheel=True :

--config=wheel_common is required, and the build fails at build time without it. The config sets --//:wheel_build=True , which routes the shared XLA/MLIR backend through the torch_version -reset transition so that pywrap factors it into a single libxla_base.so ; built without the flag, every per-version common ships its own copy of the backend and the resulting wheel aborts on import torch with duplicate static registrations.

wheel_common also turns on the Remote Build Execution (RBE) remote cache and remote executor. If you do not have RBE credentials, append --config=no_rbe to strip those flags back out:

The order matters here: --config=no_rbe has to come after --config=wheel_common , because the later config is the one that wins for the remote-cache and remote-executor flags they both set.

Note that installing without --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu will install the CUDA version of torch ; pass --extra-index-url as shown above or install the CPU build separately.

The project uses Bazel for dependency management. Key Python dependencies are:

This project uses Bazel for building and dependency management.

To install Bazel, we actually install Bazelisk, which is a transparent wrapper that handles downloading and installing Bazel itself.

There are several ways to install Bazelisk. Here are some common ways:

To verify the install, run bazel info in the repo's root directory:

For C++ code navigation, it is recommended to use VSCode with clangd extension . Relying on a compilation database generated from Bazel action graph, clangd is able to enrich the editor with various smart features, including code completions, go-to definitions, etc.

It may take a while (> 30 minutes) for the first run to make a full build, but reruns will be incremental and cheap. If you have run bazel build recently, generated files already exist so you can pass --no-build to skip waiting for heavy builds (note that on a fresh workspace, skipping the build may prevent clangd from resolving generated files). See more options in the script file-level comments.

Alternatively, you can invoke the script via nox (arguments after -- are forwarded):

items.title: Al via la maxi causa Mediaset-Berlusconi contro Corona. Lui: 'Non ho paura'
items.summary: Chiesti 160 milioni anche da Scotti, De Filippi e altri. Un ex collaboratore lo attacca
items.content:
"Mi prendo la responsabilità di tutto ciò che ho detto, non ho paura". Così Fabrizio Corona uscendo dalla prima udienza, davanti al Tribunale civile di Milano, della maxi causa intentata contro di lui dal gruppo Mediaset, da Pier Silvio e Marina Berlusconi, da Maria De Filippi, Silvia Toffanin, Gerry Scotti, Ilary Blasi e Samira Lui. E con una richiesta danni "reputazionali e patrimoniali", per una "campagna di odio" e diffamazione, da 160 milioni di euro in totale, in particolare per una puntata del 26 gennaio del podcast "Falsissimo" dell'ex agente fotografico.

I legali del gruppo, dei vertici e dei conduttori (non presenti in aula), gli avvocati Andrea Di Porto, Giulia Bongiorno e Salvatore Pino, hanno discusso, davanti alla giudice Stefania Novelli, assieme ai legali dell'ex fotografo dei vip e della società Atena, gli avvocati Piergiorgio Molinari, Umberto Ilardo e Laura Bertani. Questi ultimi hanno chiesto di non ammettere una serie di prove richieste dall'altra parte e la giudice nei prossimi giorni depositerà un'ordinanza.

Nel caso di ammissione il procedimento civile andrà avanti con altre udienze, altrimenti si arriverà subito a una decisione. In una memoria, depositata nelle scorse settimane dai legali dei promotori della causa, sono state confermate le richieste danni a carico dell'ex "re dei paparazzi". Corona, hanno scritto i legali, "si pone deliberatamente al di fuori di qualsivoglia contesto regolamentato, sfruttando i vuoti normativi connessi ai nuovi mezzi di comunicazione, per provare a operare 'legibus solutus', svincolato da qualsiasi regola etica e deontologica". Corona, nel frattempo, ha attaccato gli avvocati di Mediaset, dei vertici e dei conduttori davanti ai cronisti. E pure dentro l'aula nell'udienza a porte chiuse.

"Mi chiedono una cifra che è fuori dalle tabelle del Tribunale e questo è un reato", ha detto ancora, ribadendo, come già annunciato tempo fa, di aver presentato una denuncia per estorsione. L'avvocato Ilardo, che assiste Atena anch'essa citata in causa, ha spiegato di aver sollevato la questione di "mezzi di prova" depositati fuori dai termini in "violazione delle regole del contraddittorio".

Intanto, proprio nel giorno dell'udienza è spuntata su YouTube una puntata intitolata "Falsissimo-speciale 'Tutta la verità'" in cui un tale "Ben", che si presenta come ex collaboratore di Corona e che lo ha aiutato a costruire quella "macchina" on line da "milioni di euro", punta a smascherare punto per punto - con telefonate e conversazioni dell'ex agente fotografico registrate di nascosto e in parte pubblicate - proprio i metodi del creatore del podcast. E i suoi meccanismi di "manipolazione" in cui "realtà e finzione" si mescolano. Dice di avere "20 terabyte in un hardisk custodito in una cassetta di sicurezza", mette in fila uno a uno i retroscena del "sistema" costruito dall'ex fotografo dei vip e spiega di essere pronto a mettere a disposizione il suo archivio con tutte le registrazioni.

Sempre negli atti dei legali di Mediaset si legge che Corona ha spacciato "per verità assoluta accuse e insinuazioni gravemente diffamatorie, costruite sul nulla". E "fuori da qui, sui social, in televisione e nei locali, continua, con lo stesso accanimento, la stessa violenza verbale, la stessa prepotenza, a propalare le medesime invettive, accuse e insinuazioni". Gli eventuali risarcimenti, aveva già spiegato il gruppo, serviranno "alla creazione di un fondo per la copertura delle spese di assistenza legale delle vittime di stalking, dei reati rientranti nel cosiddetto Codice Rosso e di tutti i fenomeni di cyberbullismo".

items.title: Modella fan di Bolsonaro diventa virale, ma è creata dall'IA
items.summary: Julia è giovane, bionda e ha mezzo milione di followers. Ma non esiste
items.content:
Nella campagna brasiliana la destra si inventa i testimonial. Da settimane il candidato trumpiano Flavio Bolsonaro appare in video ormai virali mentre balla con una modella molto bella, una sorta di influencer, Julia Berlli Cortez, con ben 500mila follower. Ma nelle ultime ore si è scoperto che questa ragazza, che secondo la sua biografia su Istragram ha 22 anni, e studia medicina, semplicemente non esiste. E' un prodotto dell'intelligenza artificiale.

Un vero e proprio testimonial creato in laboratorio, visto che questa ragazza è stata intervistata e i suoi interventi sono diventati popolarissimi in rete. Per renderla più credibile, oltre a postare decine di selfie allo specchio, ha postato anche storie sui suoi social di suoi presunti fidanzati, come avrebbe fatto qualsiasi ragazza della sua età. Ma tutto è assolutamente falso.

Peccato per Bolsonaro e il suo staff che alcuni debunker, persone specializzate a trovare i profili fake, l'hanno scoperta. I falsari hanno fatto alcuni errori: nei video mentre partecipa alle manifestazioni politiche ha sempre lo stesso vestito, e spesso è scalza. Particolari che hanno fatto scattare i sospetti e che alla fine hanno portato a scoprire la verità.

In un'intervista, lei spiega sorridente perchè è di destra. Peccato che quella intervista e quelle parole non erano le sue, ma esattamente quelle pronunciate da una militante, sempre bolsonarista, ma decisamente molto meno attraente. Insomma, la strategia è semplice ed efficace: grazie alla creazione di un profilo finto, di una bella ragazza, si produce la confezione perfetta per attirare contatti e followers in modo da veicolare meglio i propri contenuti.

Infine, particolare piccante che rende la storia ancora più triste: i creatori di questo profilo non si sono limitati a lavorare nel settore della propaganda politica, ma hanno anche cercato di ottenere un po' di soldi su un altro fronte: cliccando sul canale telegram di questa ragazza e pagando 30-40 reales, meno di dieci euro, è possibile vedere suoi contenuti porno, ovviamente anche questi completamente falsi.

items.title: Voxtral 3
items.summary: Article URL: https://mistral.ai/news/voxtral-3/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50168396 Points: 619 # Comments: 156
items.content:
Merci de recevoir ce patient pour un avis dermatologique. Traitement en cours : crème à l’hydrocortisone. Dr Martin, Clinique du Parc.

It says, "Merci de recevoir ce patient pour un avis dermatologique." Your doctor is asking a dermatologist, Dr Martin, to see you. The next slot is Tuesday at 5:45 pm. Shall I book it?

Done. Bring the letter, your carte Vitale, and I'll text you the details in English.

Hi, my doctor gave me a referral letter in French. Can you book it for me?

Voxtral 3 introduces a cutting-edge voice agent SDK and state-of-the-art speech models designed for real-time, multi-step conversations across 50+ languages. It combines accurate transcription, natural speech synthesis with emotional adaptability, and deep tool integration for seamless workflow automation. Available via Mistral’s EU-hosted API or self-deployment, it ensures data sovereignty while delivering low-latency, human-like interactions for contact centers, virtual assistants, and hands-free copilots.

Speech transcription and voice generation have come a long way, but building end-to-end voice agents that can listen, reason, interact, and handle complex workflows remains difficult.

A reliable voice agent needs to do four things very well (and simultaneously):

Listen accurately across languages, accents, speakers, and interruptions,

Getting all four to work together reliably in real time remains a challenge.

To address this, we introduce Voxtral 3: a new family of state-of-the-art speech-to-text and text-to-speech models, alongside a voice agent SDK that brings listening, thinking, tool calling, and speaking into a single real-time streaming pipeline.

Voxtral 3 is built to create natural conversational experiences, from contact-center agents and service desks to virtual assistants and hands-free copilots. With support for dozens of languages, expressive speech, complex reasoning, and deep integration with your own tools and data, agents built with Voxtral can interpret nuanced intent, reason through sophisticated requests, and execute multi-step actions across connected systems.

As with other Mistral models, the Voxtral 3 family is designed for sovereign deployment. Available today through Mistral's EU-hosted API or for self-deployment on your own infrastructure, it gives organizations control over where audio is processed, how data is handled, and whether conversations are retained.

Accurate transcription across 50+ languages . The speech-to-text model, Voxtral Small Transcribe 3 , is state-of-the-art in multilingual transcription, identifying who said what (diarization), using keyphrases to improve its accuracy (context-biasing). It detects when someone has finished speaking so agents can respond without delay (end-of-turn detection).

Natural speech that adapts to the conversation . The text-to-speech model, Voxtral Mini TTS 3 , introduces new voices that adjust their emotion, pace, and emphasis based on conversational context, with support for 35+ languages and 50+ dialects.

Human-like intelligence at your (spoken) command . The new voice agent SDK combines listening, reasoning, tool calling, and speaking into a real-time experience. Agents can retrieve information, interact with business systems, and complete tasks during live conversations over phone or web.

Pro Voice for distinctly accurate voice adaptation . For professional use cases where basic voice cloning does not suffice, Voxtral’s Pro Voice adaptation is able to reproduce a speaker’s distinctive character, emotional range, and speaking style across languages, using just 30 minutes of audio.

Your voice AI, on your infrastructure . Use Mistral's EU-hosted API or deploy Voxtral 3 on your own infrastructure. Keep sensitive conversations within your environment and control whether any audio is retained.

Voxtral Transcribe 3 represents a significant milestone across transcription, diarization (who spoke when) and context biasing capabilities. The supported list of languages is expanded to 50, including 24 official EU languages and many low-resource Asian and Indic languages.

The Small version achieves state-of-the-art results across diarization and multilingual transcription, including in English, French and Spanish. It outperforms Whisper, Scribe v2 and Gemini 3.5 Transcribe. The Mini variant is 4B parameters, enabling fast and accurate transcriptions at a price of $0.0035/min.

Both models support context biasing, where key terms and free-form text can be given to bias the transcription and improve recall on technical terms. This enables them to be used in production settings with domain-specific vocabulary without the need for fine-tuning.

Voxtral Realtime Transcribe 3 is a realtime transcription model built for agentic use-cases. It achieves high-quality transcriptions at sub-500ms latency in over 35 languages, including with diarization and context biasing.

End-of-turn prediction is natively supported, incorporating both acoustic and semantic information to accurately predict when a user is finished speaking. This allows for low-latency voice agent applications, while minimizing false cut-off rates when the user is prematurely interrupted.

Voxtral Mini TTS 3.0 , available in batch and realtime, achieves state-of-the-art expressiveness and instruction following for 35+ languages and 50+ dialects. At $13 per 1M characters, Voxtral Speech 3 costs less to run than comparable models from OpenAI TTS-1, Deepgram, ElevenLabs Flash and Gemini Flash.

The speech model implicitly interprets the semantic meaning of context better, producing natural speech across a diverse range of emotions and languages. New and improved features include voice cloning from 30+ minutes of sampled audio, custom prompt instruction following (IF), contextual TTS, and a vocabulary library, all of which serve the goal of speech reliability in deployment. Variables for Explicit IF include emotion , pacing , and emphasis .

items.title: Sixteen years after Deepwater Horizon, deep sea life shows few signs of recovery
items.summary: Article URL: https://e360.yale.edu/digest/deepwater-horizon-deep-sea-recovery Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50168357 Points: 249 # Comments: 151
items.content:
Sixteen years after an explosion on the Deepwater Horizon oil rig unleashed more than 4 million barrels of oil into the Gulf of Mexico, life in the deep sea has yet to recover.

A new study finds that in the first few years after the 2010 disaster, populations of octopus, squid, krill, shrimp, and lanternfish declined by at least 60 percent. The research, based on acoustic surveys and thousands of netted samples across a broad swath of the Gulf of Mexico, found little evidence that life in the deep sea has bounced back.

The study, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences , described the losses as “the fastest and most severe” decline of animal life in the ocean layer that extends from about 600 feet deep to more than two miles down. While researchers stopped short of concluding that the oil spill had caused the declines, they said it was “the most parsimonious explanation.”

Since the disaster, scientists have found oil-related compounds in the flesh of squid and octopus and in fish eggs deep underwater, contamination that they say can impair reproduction and development or lead to an early death. Lingering pollution may make it harder for deep-sea fish that are guided by their sense of smell to find mates.

Beyond the drop in population numbers, the new study also found some declines in genetic diversity. The risk, authors say, is that populations may not harbor the genetic traits needed to survive in a rapidly changing world.

items.title: Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast
items.summary: Janine Lochrenberg, 65, was out on her daily morning swim with her club when she was attacked, her family tell the BBC.
items.content:
A South African woman has been killed in a shark attack off the country's east coast, in what is the first recorded such fatality this year.

Janine Lochrenberg was swimming off a beach in KuGompo City (formerly East London) on Tuesday morning when she was attacked.

Witnesses said the 65-year-old was bitten in two places and died before she was brought to shore.

Shark attacks are rare in South Africa, with about 10 fatal ones since 2012, according to the Florida Museum's International Shark Attack File.

Lochrenberg was out on a daily morning swim with her local open water swimming club when she was attacked at around 08:00 (06:00 GMT). Fellow swimmers brought her to shore, but it's believed she died before they could get her out of the water.

She was bitten on her thigh and her upper arm, one of her fellow swimmers told the BBC. They also said she had been wearing a magnetic shark repellent band on her ankle at the time.

Lochrenberg's sister Margot said she was holding her sister's head as they brought her to shore but believed she bled out in the water.

She told the BBC that her sister had "loved the water so much" despite knowing there was an "elevated shark presence in East London".

"She'd made peace with that. She had a deep affinity with the water and was a remarkable person," she said.

Barbara Briceland, Lochrenberg's partner, told the BBC the retired medical physicist was a good swimmer, who often swam far out into the breakers, and described her as very brave.

"She was highly intelligent, lots of fun, kind, in a quietish way, thoughtful, well-loved with a love of life."

Briceland added they were looking forward to retirement and were about to leave for a three-week road trip together.

Orient Beach, where the attack took place, has been closed alongside another nearby beach, authorities confirmed.

items.title: Garmin Edge 1060 è il nuovo ciclocomputer che si controlla senza togliere le mani dal manubrio
items.summary: Garmin annuncia tre nuovi ciclocomputer della gamma Edge, il top di gamma Edge 1060 e i nuovi Edge Explore 3 ed Edge Explore 3 Plus. Il top di gamma si controlla completamente con la voce, si integra con TrainPeaks e permette anche di ricaricare smartphone e luci ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Garmin rinnova la propria gamma di ciclocomputer annunciando tre nuovi modelli che introducono come principale novità l'integrazione di microfono e altoparlante sul manubrio.

In cima all'offerta si posiziona il nuovo Garmin Edge 1060 , top di gamma pensato per gli utenti più esigenti e per chi cerca strumenti di analisi avanzati. La caratteristica distintiva del modello è il supporto ai comandi vocali diretti : tramite il comando “OK, Garmin” è possibile richiedere informazioni sulle metriche di corsa, navigare verso punti di interesse o inviare segnalazioni di ostacoli e buche senza mai staccare le mani dal manubrio. Oltre ai comandi, l'hardware audio integrato permette la riproduzione ad alta voce delle indicazioni turn-by-turn e la gestione dei messaggi vocali bidirezionali tramite l'applicazione Garmin Messenger.

Sul fronte dell'interfaccia, Edge 1060 affianca al display touch una serie di tasti fisici pensati per agevolare il controllo con i guanti o sotto la pioggia . Il pacchetto software include funzioni come la gestione della Stamina in tempo reale, le indicazioni di potenza tramite Power Guide, il rilevamento avanzato delle uscite di gruppo GroupRide e l'integrazione con i piani di allenamento di TrainingPeaks (piattaforma che ricordiamo Garmin ha acquisito la scorsa estate). La batteria garantisce fino a 20 ore di autonomia in condizioni di uso intenso, estendibili a 60 in risparmio energetico, e supporta la ricarica inversa tramite porta USB-C per alimentare dispositivi esterni o luci compatibili.

Per chi cerca una soluzione orientata soprattutto alla navigazione e alla cicloturistica arrivano invece i nuovi modelli della serie Explore. Il modello base, Garmin Edge Explore 3 , punta sull'essenzialità e sull'efficienza di calcolo dei percorsi. Offre un display touchscreen e mappe dettagliate che suggeriscono itinerari alternativi in base al tipo di bici o al dislivello, notificando pericoli segnalati dalla community e punti di interesse lungo la traccia tramite la funzione Up Ahead. A livello di allenamento integra il supporto a Garmin Cycling Coach con programmi adattivi per principianti, garantendo la compatibilità con le e-bike per il monitoraggio della carica e un'autonomia dichiarata che raggiunge le 16 ore in uso intenso e 48 ore in risparmio energetico.

L' Edge Explore 3 Plus riprende la medesima impostazione costruttiva e le funzioni cartografiche dell'Explore 3, ma aggiunge il comparto audio con altoparlante e microfono integrati. A differenza dell'Edge 1060 non dispone dei comandi vocali completi per il controllo del dispositivo, ma sfrutta il microfono per consentire l'invio e la ricezione di messaggi vocali via Garmin Messenger. L'altoparlante integrato riproduce le indicazioni stradali e gli aggiornamenti di navigazione, oltre a poter essere utilizzato come campanello digitale per segnalare la propria presenza. A causa del maggior consumo legato alle componenti audio, l'autonomia massima in modalità di uso intenso per la versione Plus scende leggermente a 14 ore, mantenendo comunque le 48 ore in risparmio energetico.

Anche sul versante dei dei dispositivi per ciclisti, prezzi in salita rispetto ai modelli precedenti Garmin, con rincari tra i 100 e i 200 euro: l'Edge 1060 ha un prezzo di 799,99 euro (l’Edge 1040 partiva da 599,99), mentre per la serie Explore si parte dai 399,99 euro dell'Edge Explore 3 (l’Explore 2 costava 299,99 euro) per arrivare ai 499,99 euro per la versione Explore 3 Plus.

items.title: Bonus mamme 2026, al via le domande. Come presentarle: le cose da sapere
items.summary: L'Inps comunica l'apertura alle richieste per il beneficio
items.content:
Via libera alle domande per il bonus mamme per il 2026 : l'Inps comunica l'apertura alle richieste per il beneficio che consiste in un'integrazione al reddito pari a 60 euro mensili per ciascun mese o frazione di mese di vigenza del rapporto di lavoro o dell'attività di lavoro autonomo nel 2026, fino a un massimo di dodici mensilità e a un importo complessivo massimo di 720 euro.

Il servizio per la presentazione della domanda è disponibile sul sito istituzionale www.inps.it .

Bonus Mamme - La circolare INPS numero 106 del 16 ottobre 2026

Dopo l'autenticazione, utilizzando la propria identità digitale si accede al "Punto d'accesso alle prestazioni non pensionistiche" per la compilazione della richiesta. La domanda può essere presentata anche tramite il Contact Center Multicanale , contattando il numero verde 803.164, gratuito da rete fissa, o il numero 06 164.164 da rete mobile, a pagamento.

La domanda deve essere presentata entro il 31 dicembre 2026 . Nel caso in cui il requisito si perfezioni nel mese di dicembre 2026, la domanda potrà essere presentata entro il 31 gennaio 2027 .

Il beneficio non spetta indistintamente a tutte le lavoratrici. Per le madri con due figli è necessario che il più piccolo non abbia ancora compiuto dieci anni . Per quelle con almeno tre figli , invece, il limite di età del figlio più piccolo è fissato a 18 anni . È inoltre richiesto che il reddito annuo da lavoro, dipendente o autonomo, non superi 40.000 euro .

Le mensilità spettanti per il periodo dal 1° gennaio 2026 al 31 dicembre 2026 sono corrisposte in unica soluzione nel mese di dicembre 2026, contestualmente alla mensilità riferita al medesimo mese, qualora l'istruttoria sia definita in tempo utile.

L'avvio dell'istruttoria avviene sulla base della data di presentazione della domanda. Qualora l'istruttoria non possa essere conclusa in tempo utile per il pagamento nel mese di dicembre, le somme spettanti saranno corrisposte, all'esito della relativa definizione, a decorrere dal mese di gennaio 2027 .

items.title: Una foto con gli occhi chiusi? Lightroom su mobile li apre con un tocco, usando l’IA
items.summary: Su iPhone, iPad e Android debutta la funzione Open Eyes: se qualcuno ha battuto le palpebre al momento dello scatto, l’IA generativa ricostruisce gli occhi ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Una foto riuscita, se non fosse per quella persona che ha chiuso gli occhi proprio al momento dello scatto. Adobe vuole risolvere uno degli inconvenienti più comuni della fotografia con Open Eyes, nuova funzione della versione mobile di Lightroom che utilizza l’Intelligenza Artificiale generativa per aprire gli occhi dei soggetti con un solo tocco.

La novità è disponibile nella versione di Lightroom per iOS, iPadOS e Android e non richiede una selezione manuale particolarmente elaborata.

Quando l’applicazione individua uno o più soggetti con gli occhi chiusi, propone automaticamente Open Eyes tra le azioni rapide, mostrando direttamente sulla fotografia l’icona dalla quale avviare la correzione. A quel punto è l’IA a generare il risultato, cercando di mantenere coerenti illuminazione, posizione del viso e caratteristiche della persona.

Ok, ma come fa Adobe a sapere come sono gli occhi di una persona se sono chiusi? Se nella libreria di Lightroom sono presenti altre immagini della stessa persona, Open Eyes può utilizzarle come riferimento per cercare di riprodurre più accuratamente colore, forma e dimensione degli occhi.

Altrimenti, di fatto, il sistema di Lightroom ricostruisce degli occhi credibili ma che molto probabilmente non corrisponderanno (per colore, per esempio) a quelli del soggetto della foto.

Photoshop Elements offre da anni una funzione simile, ma con un approccio differente: il software può prendere gli occhi da un'altra fotografia della stessa persona e utilizzarli per correggere lo scatto. Il risultato dipende quindi anche da quanto le due immagini siano compatibili per posizione del viso, luce ed espressione.

Anche Photoshop permette già di raggiungere risultati simili attraverso i suoi strumenti generativi, ma richiede un intervento più articolato. In Lightroom Adobe sta cercando di trasformare la stessa operazione in una funzione automatica accessibile direttamente dall'interfaccia mobile.

Open Eyes è una funzione gratuita, ma ci sono dei limiti sebbene Adobe non sia chiara in merito. Secondo quanto riportato da DPReview , gli utenti della versione gratuita possono provare Open Eyes due volte; al terzo tentativo viene proposta la sottoscrizione di un piano Adobe Creative Cloud che comprenda ulteriori crediti per le funzioni basate sull'IA.
